title: Native lint path
caption: How ordinary source and TSRX source reach OXC, then map safe results back to original TSRX bytes.

nodes.ordinary: Ordinary JavaScript and TypeScript bypass the TSRX scanner and go directly to the OXC parser.
nodes.tsrx: The native lint path starts with the exact authored TSRX bytes.
nodes.scan: A linear structural scan recognizes TSRX syntax while protecting strings, comments, templates, JSX text, and Unicode bytes.
nodes.overlay: The scanner stores structure and original spans in compact flat vectors instead of a second tree.
nodes.projection: TSRX controls become legal TSX scaffolding while authored descendant ranges stay byte-for-byte unchanged.
nodes.buffer_map: One projected buffer carries sorted identity segments that connect copied ranges to the original source.
nodes.parser: OXC parses the original ordinary source or the legal TSX projection once.
nodes.arena: The OXC program keeps one arena-backed AST whose spans address the projected source bytes.
nodes.lint: OXC semantic analysis and oxlint rules run on the single parsed program.
nodes.translate: A label or fix maps back only when its complete range stays inside one authored identity segment.
nodes.diagnostics: Accepted labels and fixes point to the original TSRX. Unsafe synthetic or cross-segment results are suppressed or rejected.

steps.label: Scan
steps.caption: One linear scan reads your TSRX bytes and records every control and its original span in a compact overlay.

steps.label: Project
steps.caption: TSRX controls become legal TSX scaffolding in one projected buffer, and an identity map ties every copied range back to your original bytes.

steps.label: OXC
steps.caption: Ordinary files and the projection take the same road: one OXC parse, one arena AST, then semantic analysis and oxlint rules.

steps.label: Map back
steps.caption: Results are translated onto your original TSRX bytes. Anything that cannot be mapped safely is suppressed instead of guessed.
